Ibn Muqbil said:

"And time is but two turns: by one I die, and by the other I seek life, toiling."

[[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 21/40.]]

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: Musa related to us, saying: Ibn 'Alawiyya related to us, saying: Isma'il related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bishr related to us from Sufyan al-Thawri, from his father, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The regretful one awaits mercy, the self-admirer awaits aversion, and every doer will come upon what he has done before" [114] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 15/936, no. 43607.]].

He said: "That is the presentation (al-'ardh); but whoever is scrutinized in the reckoning will be punished" [115] [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/127.]].

﴿But as for him who is given his book behind his back﴾: his right hand will be shackled to his neck and his left hand placed behind his back, so his book will be given to him with his left hand from behind his back. Mujahid said: his hand will be dislocated behind his back.

﴿He will call out for destruction﴾, i.e., he will be summoned with woe and ruin, ﴿and he will burn in a blaze﴾. Abu Ja'far, Ayyub, and the Kufans other than al-Kisa'i read it with a fatha on the ya' and light (tashdid-less) pronunciation, and Abu 'Ubayd preferred it because of His saying: ﴿except him who is to burn in Hell﴾ [[Surat al-Saffat: 163.]], and His saying: ﴿who will burn in the greatest Fire﴾ [[Surat al-A'la: 12.]]. The rest read it with a damma on the ya' and a shadda on the lam, and Abu Hatim preferred it because of His saying: ﴿Then into Hell roast him﴾ [[Surat al-Haqqa: 31.]], and ﴿and the burning of Hell﴾ [[Surat al-Waqi'a: 94.]]. ﴿He used to be among his people, rejoicing﴾. I heard al-Sulami say: I heard Mansur ibn 'Abd Allah say: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Misri say: Ibn 'Ata said of himself: "pursuing, striving."

﴿He thought that he would never return﴾, i.e., return to Us.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I seek refuge in You from returning after having been in order (al-kawr)" [116] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/148.]]. Ibn 'Abbas said: "I did not know the meaning of yahur until I heard a Bedouin woman calling to her daughter, saying: 'Hawri, hawri!' meaning: return." And the poet said:

"A man is but like a spark and its light: it returns to ashes after having blazed."

[[al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/330.]]

Then He said: ﴿Yes﴾, meaning: it is not as he thought. ﴿Yes, he will return to Us and be resurrected.﴾ ﴿Indeed, his Lord was ever seeing of him.﴾

﴿So I swear by twilight (al-shafaq)﴾. Mujahid and others said: it is the whole day. 'Ikrima said: what remains of the day. Ibn 'Abbas and most people said: it is the redness that remains on the horizon after the sun sets, and with its disappearance the beginning of the time of the late evening prayer (al-'isha') becomes due. Among the Companions who held this view were Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn al-Zubayr, 'Umar and his son, 'Ubada ibn al-Samit, Shaddad ibn Aws, Anas ibn Malik, Abu Qatada al-Ansari, Abu Hurayra and Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah. Among the Successors were Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Tawus, 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar and Makhul. Among the jurists were Malik, al-Awza'i, al-Shafi'i, Abu Yusuf, Abu Thawr, Ibn 'Ubayd, Ahmad and Ishaq. Others said: it is the whiteness, and this was the view of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz and Abu Hanifa. The preferred view is the first, because the scholars of the 'Abadila (Ibn 'Abbas's circle of Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Umar, Ibn al-Zubayr and Ibn 'Amr) agreed upon it, and because the evidences in Arabic speech and poetry attest to it. Al-Farra' said: I heard some Arabs say: "The thawr is red, as if it were the shafaq." And a poet said:

"Red in color, like the reddening of the twilight."

And another said:

"Rise, O boy, serving me without shame before time, with a cup filled with twilight."

[[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/303; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/275, where the text reads "murtabik" for "muhtashim".]]

The hollow is also called shafaq. The philosophers assert that whiteness never disappears at all. Al-Khalil said: "I climbed the minaret of Alexandria and looked at the whiteness, and I saw it moving from horizon to horizon, and I never saw it set." And God knows best what is correct.

﴿And by the night and what it gathers (wa-ma wasaq)﴾, i.e., what it gathers and assembles. It is said: wasaqtuhu, asiquhu, wasqan, and from it is said of a great collected quantity of food: wasq, which is sixty sa'; and a food that is wasq is one gathered into a sack or container. Mujahid said, according to the narration of Ibn Abi Najih: "what harbors in it of creatures." Mansur related from him: "what wraps and darkens upon it and enters into it." 'Ikrima: "what it has gathered in it of its creatures, scorpions, serpents, and its darkness." Al-Dahhak and Muqatil: "what it drives of its darkness; when night comes, every thing goes back to its shelter." Al-Ustadh Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib said: it is possible that on this view it is inverted (maqlub), because the root of saqa is yasuqu. 'Uthman: "it carries from the darkness." Abu Hayyan: "it comes from darkness or a star." Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "what it has worked in it." Ibn Abi Mulayka and Ibn Jubayr related from Ibn 'Abbas: "what it gathers," and he said: "Have you not heard the poet's saying:

'Indeed for us are she-camels, noble, gathered, which, if they found a driver, would be driven together.'"

[[Tafsir Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/150; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/277; Lisan al-'Arab: 10/380.]]

﴿By the moon when it becomes full (idha ittasaq)﴾, i.e., when it gathers, aligns, and its light is complete. Qatada: "when it becomes round." It is also said: "it travels." Murra al-Hamdani: "it rises, and that is in the bright nights." It is said: ittasaqa al-shay' when it follows in succession, and istawsaqa al-ibl when the camels gather and join together; it is an ifta'ala form from al-wasq.

﴿You will surely embark (la-tarkabunna)﴾: the readers of Mecca and Kufa, except 'Asim, read it with a fatha on the ta', and this is the reading of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ibn Mas'ud and his companions, Ibn 'Abbas and Abu al-'Aliya. They said: it means, O Muhammad, you will ascend heaven after heaven, degree after degree, and rank after rank. It was also said: it refers to the sky changing color after color, becoming at times like molten brass (al-dihan) and at times like dregs of oil (al-muhl), and being split open with the clouds at one time and folded (in the Tabari: "reddened") at another [[See Tafsir al-Tabari: 30/155.]]. The others read it with a damma and preferred it, Abu 'Ubayd said: "because the meaning is more apt for people than for the Prophet (ﷺ). Before the verse He mentioned those from among them who are given their book in their right or left hand, then He said after it: ﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe?﴾ and mentioned their mounting of layer upon layer, between them."

The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of the verse. Most of them said: state after state and matter after matter in the stations of the Resurrection, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from al-Kalbi. Hayyan from him: "at one time they recognize, at another they are ignorant." Muqatil: "that is death, then life, then death, then life." 'Ata: "at one time poverty, at another wealth." 'Amr ibn Dinar from Ibn 'Abbas: "the hardships and terrors: death, then resurrection, then the reckoning." The Arabs say of one who has fallen into a severe matter: "he has fallen into the daughters of Tabaq, and then into another set of daughters of Tabaq." Abu 'Ubayda: "you will embark upon the ways and conditions of those who came before you and of your own states." 'Ikrima: "state after state." (Another report:) an infant, then a weaned child, then a youth, then a young man, then an old man. The philosophers said: a human passes through, from being a drop of semen until he grows old and dies, thirty-seven states corresponding to thirty-seven names: a drop, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, then another creation, then a fetus, then a newborn, then a suckling, then one weaned, then a youth (yafi'), then one growing up (nash'), then one who is shooting up (mutara'ri'), then a hazur (a boy when he has grown strong and become capable of service; see Lisan al-'Arab: 4/187), then one approaching puberty (murahiq), then one who has reached maturity (muhtalim), then an adult (baligh), then a beardless youth (amrad), then one whose beard has begun (tarid), then one whose beard has come in (tari), then one with a sprouting beard (baqil), then one who has taken control (musaytir), then one whose face is full (mutarkhim), then one whose beard is thick (mukhtat), then one with a full beard (sumul), then one with a bearded face (multihin), then one who has come to his full stature (mustawi), then one who has risen (mus'id), then one who has gathered his strength (mujtami'), and the young man comprises all of this; then one who is struck (malhuz), then an elder (kahl), then one whose hair is white mixed with black (ashmat), then an old man (shaykh), then one with white hair (ashyab), then one who is bent (hawqal), then one who is bent double (saftana), then one who is decrepit (haram), then a dead person (mayyit). This is the meaning of His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿You will surely embark﴾.

﴿Stage after stage (tabaqan 'an tabaq)﴾. The word tabaq in the language means state. Al-Aqra' ibn Habis said:

"I am a man who has milked the years' flanks, and the years have driven me from one tabaq to another.
So I do not yearn for a companion who will part from me, nor does my inner being shrink from separation."

Abu al-Qasim 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Babi recited to me, saying: Abu Sa'id 'Uthman ibn Ja'far ibn Nusra al-Mawsili recited to us, saying: Abu Ya'la Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Muthanna recited to us:

"Patience is more beautiful, and the world is grieving: who among us has not tasted of its life a turbid draught?
When a tabaq of its joys is clear for you, time brings you a tabaq of its miseries."

[[Al-Ranaq: turbidity. Both verses are in Majma' al-Bayan: 10/303.]]

Makhul said concerning this verse: "Every twenty years they experience a matter they had not been in." This is the strongest proof of the createdness of the world and the affirmation of the Creator. The wise said: whoever is in one state today and another tomorrow should know that his management has been handed over to another. It was said to Abu Bakr al-Warraq: "What is the proof that this world has a Maker?" He said:

"The changing of states, the weakness of power, the frailty of limbs, the subjugation of strength, and the breaking of resolve."

I heard Abu al-Qasim the exegete say: I heard Abu al-Fadl Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Hamdun al-Nasawi say: I heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Arziyani say: Abu al-Fam 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd al-'Alawi entered upon the sick in Tabaristan and recited:

"I have become ill, though you were not ill with afflictions; thus is time, in which there is aloes and honey.
Indeed, the One whom the calamities do not touch, and whom neither time nor man changes, is God alone."

﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe? And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate?﴾ — i.e., they do not humble themselves or submit to it. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: they do not pray.

Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, by my reading to him, saying: Makki informed us by reading to him in the year three hundred and nineteen, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya related to me, saying: And in it (that year) 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Nafi' al-Madani read to me, and Mutarrif ibn 'Abd Allah related to me from Malik ibn Anas, from 'Abd Allah ibn Zayd, mawla of al-Aswad ibn Sufyan, from Abu Salama ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad, that Abu Hurayra recited ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ [[Surat al-Inshiqaq: 1.]] and prostrated in it, and when he finished he informed them that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had prostrated in it.

Abu Sa'id 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Nuh informed us, having read it to him in the year three hundred and eighty-six, saying: Abu al-'Abbas al-Siraj informed us, saying: Qutayba related to us from al-Layth, from Bakr, from Nu'aym ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad, who said: I prayed behind Abu Hurayra above this mosque, and he recited ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ and prostrated in it, and said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prostrate in it."

﴿Nay, those who disbelieve deny. And Allah knows best what they conceal (yu'una)﴾. Mujahid said: "they conceal." Qatada: "what they keep in their breasts." Ibn Zayd: "they gather from righteous and evil deeds." ﴿So give them the good news (fa-bashshirhum)﴾, i.e., inform them of ﴿a painful punishment, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward never to be cut off﴾, i.e., unreduced and uninterrupted.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 84, verses 1–25:

Makkiyya. It has twenty-five verses, one hundred and seven words, and four hundred and thirty-four letters.

Sa'id ibn Muhammad, Kamil ibn Ahmad and Muhammad ibn al-Qasim informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Mutar informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Shurayk related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us, saying: Salam ibn Sulaym related to us, saying:

Harun ibn Kathir related to us from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the Surah of Inshiqaq, Allah, glorified is He, will protect him from being given his book behind his back" [112] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/301.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿When the sky is split open﴾, and it listens to its Lord (wa-adhinat li-rabbiha), i.e., it hears the command of its Lord to split and obeys it, ﴿and it is right that it should do so﴾ (wa-huqqat), i.e., it is right for it to obey its Lord, and God has made that its duty.

﴿And when the earth is stretched out﴾, stretched like a leather hide of 'Ukaz, and its extent is increased. ﴿And casts out what is within it﴾, i.e., brings out what is in it of the dead and the treasures, ﴿and empties itself﴾, and becomes empty so that there is nothing in its interior. ﴿And it listens to its Lord and it is right that it should do so﴾. The scholars differed concerning the response (jawab) to His saying ﴿When the sky is split open﴾. It was said that its response is omitted because the meaning is understood. It was also said that its response is ﴿O man, you are toiling toward your Lord with toil, and you will meet it﴾, and its implied meaning is: when the sky is split open, every toiler will meet what he has done. Al-Mubarrad said: there is a transposition (taqdim wa-ta'khir), its intended sense being: ﴿O man, you are toiling toward your Lord with toil, and you will meet it﴾ when the sky is split open. It was also said: its response is ﴿and it listens to its Lord﴾, and in that case the waw is superfluous.

As for His saying ﴿you are toiling toward your Lord with toil﴾, the meaning is: laboring and striving toward your Lord through deeds, and you will meet Him, and you will be recompensed for it, whether good or evil. Al-Qutabi said: it means laboring in your livelihood toward the meeting with your Lord. Al-Kadh (kadh) means striving and exerting oneself in a matter until that matter leaves its mark, i.e., has an effect. From it is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever asks while he has what suffices him, his begging will come on the Day of Resurrection as scratches, or scars, or wounds on the face" [113] [[Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/589.]], i.e., the trace of a scratch. Ibn Muqbil said:

"And time is but two turns: by one I die, and by the other I seek life, toiling."

[[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 21/40.]]

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: Musa related to us, saying: Ibn 'Alawiyya related to us, saying: Isma'il related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bishr related to us from Sufyan al-Thawri, from his father, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The regretful one awaits mercy, the self-admirer awaits aversion, and every doer will come upon what he has done before" [114] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 15/936, no. 43607.]].

﴿As for him who is given his book in his right hand﴾, i.e., the register of his deeds, ﴿he will be reckoned with an easy reckoning, and he will return to his family rejoicing﴾.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Mandah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ghalib related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Sulayman related to me, saying: Mubarak ibn Fudala related to us from Ayyub, from Abu Malika, from 'A'isha, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever is reckoned with will be punished." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, has not Allah said: ﴿As for him who is given his book in his right hand, he will be reckoned with an easy reckoning﴾?" He said: "That is the presentation (al-'ardh); but whoever is scrutinized in the reckoning will be punished" [115] [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/127.]].

﴿But as for him who is given his book behind his back﴾: his right hand will be shackled to his neck and his left hand placed behind his back, so his book will be given to him with his left hand from behind his back. Mujahid said: his hand will be dislocated behind his back.

﴿He will call out for destruction﴾, i.e., he will be summoned with woe and ruin, ﴿and he will burn in a blaze﴾. Abu Ja'far, Ayyub, and the Kufans other than al-Kisa'i read it with a fatha on the ya' and light (tashdid-less) pronunciation, and Abu 'Ubayd preferred it because of His saying: ﴿except him who is to burn in Hell﴾ [[Surat al-Saffat: 163.]], and His saying: ﴿who will burn in the greatest Fire﴾ [[Surat al-A'la: 12.]]. The rest read it with a damma on the ya' and a shadda on the lam, and Abu Hatim preferred it because of His saying: ﴿Then into Hell roast him﴾ [[Surat al-Haqqa: 31.]], and ﴿and the burning of Hell﴾ [[Surat al-Waqi'a: 94.]]. ﴿He used to be among his people, rejoicing﴾. I heard al-Sulami say: I heard Mansur ibn 'Abd Allah say: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Misri say: Ibn 'Ata said of himself: "pursuing, striving."

﴿He thought that he would never return﴾, i.e., return to Us.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I seek refuge in You from returning after having been in order (al-kawr)" [116] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/148.]]. "A man is but like a spark and its light: it returns to ashes after having blazed."

[[al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/330.]]

Then He said: ﴿Yes﴾, meaning: it is not as he thought. ﴿Yes, he will return to Us and be resurrected.﴾ ﴿Indeed, his Lord was ever seeing of him.﴾

﴿So I swear by twilight (al-shafaq)﴾. Mujahid and others said: it is the whole day. 'Ikrima said: what remains of the day. Makhul said concerning this verse: "Every twenty years they experience a matter they had not been in." This is the strongest proof of the createdness of the world and the affirmation of the Creator. The wise said: whoever is in one state today and another tomorrow should know that his management has been handed over to another. It was said to Abu Bakr al-Warraq: "What is the proof that this world has a Maker?" He said:

"The changing of states, the weakness of power, the frailty of limbs, the subjugation of strength, and the breaking of resolve."

I heard Abu al-Qasim the exegete say: I heard Abu al-Fadl Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Hamdun al-Nasawi say: I heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Arziyani say: Abu al-Fam 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd al-'Alawi entered upon the sick in Tabaristan and recited:

"I have become ill, though you were not ill with afflictions; thus is time, in which there is aloes and honey.
Indeed, the One whom the calamities do not touch, and whom neither time nor man changes, is God alone."

﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe? And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate?﴾ — i.e., they do not humble themselves or submit to it. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: they do not pray.

Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, by my reading to him, saying: Makki informed us by reading to him in the year three hundred and nineteen, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya related to me, saying: And in it (that year) 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Nafi' al-Madani read to me, and Mutarrif ibn 'Abd Allah related to me from Malik ibn Anas, from 'Abd Allah ibn Zayd, mawla of al-Aswad ibn Sufyan, from Abu Salama ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad, that Abu Hurayra recited ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ [[Surat al-Inshiqaq: 1.]] and prostrated in it, and when he finished he informed them that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had prostrated in it.

Abu Sa'id 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Nuh informed us, having read it to him in the year three hundred and eighty-six, saying: Abu al-'Abbas al-Siraj informed us, saying: Qutayba related to us from al-Layth, from Bakr, from Nu'aym ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad, who said: I prayed behind Abu Hurayra above this mosque, and he recited ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ and prostrated in it, and said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prostrate in it."

﴿Nay, those who disbelieve deny. And Allah knows best what they conceal (yu'una)﴾. Mujahid said: "they conceal." Qatada: "what they keep in their breasts." Ibn Zayd: "they gather from righteous and evil deeds." ﴿So give them the good news (fa-bashshirhum)﴾, i.e., inform them of ﴿a painful punishment, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward never to be cut off﴾, i.e., unreduced and uninterrupted.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 84, verses 1–25:

Makkiyya. It has twenty-five verses, one hundred and seven words, and four hundred and thirty-four letters.

Sa'id ibn Muhammad, Kamil ibn Ahmad and Muhammad ibn al-Qasim informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Mutar informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Shurayk related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us, saying: Salam ibn Sulaym related to us, saying:

Harun ibn Kathir related to us from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the Surah of Inshiqaq, Allah, glorified is He, will protect him from being given his book behind his back" [112] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/301.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿When the sky is split open﴾, and it listens to its Lord (wa-adhinat li-rabbiha), i.e., it hears the command of its Lord to split and obeys it, ﴿and it is right that it should do so﴾ (wa-huqqat), i.e., it is right for it to obey its Lord, and God has made that its duty.

﴿And when the earth is stretched out﴾, stretched like a leather hide of 'Ukaz, and its extent is increased. ﴿And casts out what is within it﴾, i.e., brings out what is in it of the dead and the treasures, ﴿and empties itself﴾, and becomes empty so that there is nothing in its interior. ﴿And it listens to its Lord and it is right that it should do so﴾. The scholars differed concerning the response (jawab) to His saying ﴿When the sky is split open﴾. It was said that its response is omitted because the meaning is understood. It was also said that its response is ﴿O man, you are toiling toward your Lord with toil, and you will meet it﴾, and its implied meaning is: when the sky is split open, every toiler will meet what he has done. Al-Mubarrad said: there is a transposition (taqdim wa-ta'khir), its intended sense being: ﴿O man, you are toiling toward your Lord with toil, and you will meet it﴾ when the sky is split open. It was also said: its response is ﴿and it listens to its Lord﴾, and in that case the waw is superfluous.

As for His saying ﴿you are toiling toward your Lord with toil﴾, the meaning is: laboring and striving toward your Lord through deeds, and you will meet Him, and you will be recompensed for it, whether good or evil. Al-Qutabi said: it means laboring in your livelihood toward the meeting with your Lord. Al-Kadh (kadh) means striving and exerting oneself in a matter until that matter leaves its mark, i.e., has an effect. From it is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever asks while he has what suffices him, his begging will come on the Day of Resurrection as scratches, or scars, or wounds on the face" [113] [[Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/589.]], i.e., the trace of a scratch. Ibn Muqbil said:

"And time is but two turns: by one I die, and by the other I seek life, toiling."

[[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 21/40.]]

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: Musa related to us, saying: Ibn 'Alawiyya related to us, saying: Isma'il related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bishr related to us from Sufyan al-Thawri, from his father, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The regretful one awaits mercy, the self-admirer awaits aversion, and every doer will come upon what he has done before" [114] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 15/936, no. 43607.]].

﴿As for him who is given his book in his right hand﴾, i.e., the register of his deeds, ﴿he will be reckoned with an easy reckoning, and he will return to his family rejoicing﴾.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Mandah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ghalib related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Sulayman related to me, saying: Mubarak ibn Fudala related to us from Ayyub, from Abu Malika, from 'A'isha, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever is reckoned with will be punished." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, has not Allah said: ﴿As for him who is given his book in his right hand, he will be reckoned with an easy reckoning﴾?" He said: "That is the presentation (al-'ardh); but whoever is scrutinized in the reckoning will be punished" [115] [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/127.]].

﴿But as for him who is given his book behind his back﴾: his right hand will be shackled to his neck and his left hand placed behind his back, so his book will be given to him with his left hand from behind his back. Mujahid said: his hand will be dislocated behind his back.

﴿He will call out for destruction﴾, i.e., he will be summoned with woe and ruin, ﴿and he will burn in a blaze﴾. Abu Ja'far, Ayyub, and the Kufans other than al-Kisa'i read it with a fatha on the ya' and light (tashdid-less) pronunciation, and Abu 'Ubayd preferred it because of His saying: ﴿except him who is to burn in Hell﴾ [[Surat al-Saffat: 163.]], and His saying: ﴿who will burn in the greatest Fire﴾ [[Surat al-A'la: 12.]]. The rest read it with a damma on the ya' and a shadda on the lam, and Abu Hatim preferred it because of His saying: ﴿Then into Hell roast him﴾ [[Surat al-Haqqa: 31.]], and ﴿and the burning of Hell﴾ [[Surat al-Waqi'a: 94.]]. ﴿He used to be among his people, rejoicing﴾. I heard al-Sulami say: I heard Mansur ibn 'Abd Allah say: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Misri say: Ibn 'Ata said of himself: "pursuing, striving."

﴿He thought that he would never return﴾, i.e., return to Us.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I seek refuge in You from returning after having been in order (al-kawr)" [116] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/148.]]. Ibn 'Abbas said: "I did not know the meaning of yahur until I heard a Bedouin woman calling to her daughter, saying: 'Hawri, hawri!' meaning: return." And the poet said:

"A man is but like a spark and its light: it returns to ashes after having blazed."

[[al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/330.]]

Then He said: ﴿Yes﴾, meaning: it is not as he thought. ﴿Yes, he will return to Us and be resurrected.﴾ ﴿Indeed, his Lord was ever seeing of him.﴾

﴿So I swear by twilight (al-shafaq)﴾. Mujahid and others said: it is the whole day. 'Ikrima said: what remains of the day. Ibn 'Abbas and most people said: it is the redness that remains on the horizon after the sun sets, and with its disappearance the beginning of the time of the late evening prayer (al-'isha') becomes due. Among the Companions who held this view were Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn al-Zubayr, 'Umar and his son, 'Ubada ibn al-Samit, Shaddad ibn Aws, Anas ibn Malik, Abu Qatada al-Ansari, Abu Hurayra and Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah. Among the Successors were Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Tawus, 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar and Makhul. Among the jurists were Malik, al-Awza'i, al-Shafi'i, Abu Yusuf, Abu Thawr, Ibn 'Ubayd, Ahmad and Ishaq. Others said: it is the whiteness, and this was the view of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz and Abu Hanifa. The preferred view is the first, because the scholars of the 'Abadila (Ibn 'Abbas's circle of Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Umar, Ibn al-Zubayr and Ibn 'Amr) agreed upon it, and because the evidences in Arabic speech and poetry attest to it. Al-Farra' said: I heard some Arabs say: "The thawr is red, as if it were the shafaq." And a poet said:

"Red in color, like the reddening of the twilight."

And another said:

"Rise, O boy, serving me without shame before time, with a cup filled with twilight."

[[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/303; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/275, where the text reads "murtabik" for "muhtashim".]]

The hollow is also called shafaq. The philosophers assert that whiteness never disappears at all. Al-Khalil said: "I climbed the minaret of Alexandria and looked at the whiteness, and I saw it moving from horizon to horizon, and I never saw it set." And God knows best what is correct.

﴿And by the night and what it gathers (wa-ma wasaq)﴾, i.e., what it gathers and assembles. It is said: wasaqtuhu, asiquhu, wasqan, and from it is said of a great collected quantity of food: wasq, which is sixty sa'; and a food that is wasq is one gathered into a sack or container. Mujahid said, according to the narration of Ibn Abi Najih: "what harbors in it of creatures." Mansur related from him: "what wraps and darkens upon it and enters into it." 'Ikrima: "what it has gathered in it of its creatures, scorpions, serpents, and its darkness." Al-Dahhak and Muqatil: "what it drives of its darkness; when night comes, every thing goes back to its shelter." Al-Ustadh Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib said: it is possible that on this view it is inverted (maqlub), because the root of saqa is yasuqu. 'Uthman: "it carries from the darkness." Abu Hayyan: "it comes from darkness or a star." Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "what it has worked in it." Ibn Abi Mulayka and Ibn Jubayr related from Ibn 'Abbas: "what it gathers," and he said: "Have you not heard the poet's saying:

'Indeed for us are she-camels, noble, gathered, which, if they found a driver, would be driven together.'"

[[Tafsir Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/150; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/277; Lisan al-'Arab: 10/380.]]

﴿By the moon when it becomes full (idha ittasaq)﴾, i.e., when it gathers, aligns, and its light is complete. Qatada: "when it becomes round." It is also said: "it travels." Murra al-Hamdani: "it rises, and that is in the bright nights." It is said: ittasaqa al-shay' when it follows in succession, and istawsaqa al-ibl when the camels gather and join together; it is an ifta'ala form from al-wasq.

﴿You will surely embark (la-tarkabunna)﴾: the readers of Mecca and Kufa, except 'Asim, read it with a fatha on the ta', and this is the reading of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ibn Mas'ud and his companions, Ibn 'Abbas and Abu al-'Aliya. They said: it means, O Muhammad, you will ascend heaven after heaven, degree after degree, and rank after rank. It was also said: it refers to the sky changing color after color, becoming at times like molten brass (al-dihan) and at times like dregs of oil (al-muhl), and being split open with the clouds at one time and folded (in the Tabari: "reddened") at another [[See Tafsir al-Tabari: 30/155.]]. The others read it with a damma and preferred it, Abu 'Ubayd said: "because the meaning is more apt for people than for the Prophet (ﷺ). Before the verse He mentioned those from among them who are given their book in their right or left hand, then He said after it: ﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe?﴾ and mentioned their mounting of layer upon layer, between them."

The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of the verse. Most of them said: state after state and matter after matter in the stations of the Resurrection, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from al-Kalbi. Hayyan from him: "at one time they recognize, at another they are ignorant." Muqatil: "that is death, then life, then death, then life." 'Ata: "at one time poverty, at another wealth." 'Amr ibn Dinar from Ibn 'Abbas: "the hardships and terrors: death, then resurrection, then the reckoning." The Arabs say of one who has fallen into a severe matter: "he has fallen into the daughters of Tabaq, and then into another set of daughters of Tabaq." Abu 'Ubayda: "you will embark upon the ways and conditions of those who came before you and of your own states." 'Ikrima: "state after state." (Another report:) an infant, then a weaned child, then a youth, then a young man, then an old man. The philosophers said: a human passes through, from being a drop of semen until he grows old and dies, thirty-seven states corresponding to thirty-seven names: a drop, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, then another creation, then a fetus, then a newborn, then a suckling, then one weaned, then a youth (yafi'), then one growing up (nash'), then one who is shooting up (mutara'ri'), then a hazur (a boy when he has grown strong and become capable of service; see Lisan al-'Arab: 4/187), then one approaching puberty (murahiq), then one who has reached maturity (muhtalim), then an adult (baligh), then a beardless youth (amrad), then one whose beard has begun (tarid), then one whose beard has come in (tari), then one with a sprouting beard (baqil), then one who has taken control (musaytir), then one whose face is full (mutarkhim), then one whose beard is thick (mukhtat), then one with a full beard (sumul), then one with a bearded face (multihin), then one who has come to his full stature (mustawi), then one who has risen (mus'id), then one who has gathered his strength (mujtami'), and the young man comprises all of this; then one who is struck (malhuz), then an elder (kahl), then one whose hair is white mixed with black (ashmat), then an old man (shaykh), then one with white hair (ashyab), then one who is bent (hawqal), then one who is bent double (saftana), then one who is decrepit (haram), then a dead person (mayyit). This is the meaning of His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿You will surely embark﴾.

﴿Stage after stage (tabaqan 'an tabaq)﴾. The word tabaq in the language means state. Al-Aqra' ibn Habis said:

"I am a man who has milked the years' flanks, and the years have driven me from one tabaq to another.
So I do not yearn for a companion who will part from me, nor does my inner being shrink from separation."

Abu al-Qasim 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Babi recited to me, saying: Abu Sa'id 'Uthman ibn Ja'far ibn Nusra al-Mawsili recited to us, saying: Abu Ya'la Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Muthanna recited to us:

"Patience is more beautiful, and the world is grieving: who among us has not tasted of its life a turbid draught?
When a tabaq of its joys is clear for you, time brings you a tabaq of its miseries."

[[Al-Ranaq: turbidity. Both verses are in Majma' al-Bayan: 10/303.]]

Makhul said concerning this verse: "Every twenty years they experience a matter they had not been in." This is the strongest proof of the createdness of the world and the affirmation of the Creator. The wise said: whoever is in one state today and another tomorrow should know that his management has been handed over to another. It was said to Abu Bakr al-Warraq: "What is the proof that this world has a Maker?" He said:

"The changing of states, the weakness of power, the frailty of limbs, the subjugation of strength, and the breaking of resolve."

I heard Abu al-Qasim the exegete say: I heard Abu al-Fadl Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Hamdun al-Nasawi say: I heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Arziyani say: Abu al-Fam 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd al-'Alawi entered upon the sick in Tabaristan and recited:

"I have become ill, though you were not ill with afflictions; thus is time, in which there is aloes and honey.
Indeed, the One whom the calamities do not touch, and whom neither time nor man changes, is God alone."

﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe? And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate?﴾ — i.e., they do not humble themselves or submit to it. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: they do not pray.

Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, by my reading to him, saying: Makki informed us by reading to him in the year three hundred and nineteen, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya related to me, saying: And in it (that year) 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Nafi' al-Madani read to me, and Mutarrif ibn 'Abd Allah related to me from Malik ibn Anas, from 'Abd Allah ibn Zayd, mawla of al-Aswad ibn Sufyan, from Abu Salama ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad, that Abu Hurayra recited ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ [[Surat al-Inshiqaq: 1.]] and prostrated in it, and when he finished he informed them that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had prostrated in it.

Abu Sa'id 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Nuh informed us, having read it to him in the year three hundred and eighty-six, saying: Abu al-'Abbas al-Siraj informed us, saying: Qutayba related to us from al-Layth, from Bakr, from Nu'aym ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad, who said: I prayed behind Abu Hurayra above this mosque, and he recited ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ and prostrated in it, and said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prostrate in it."

﴿Nay, those who disbelieve deny. And Allah knows best what they conceal (yu'una)﴾. Mujahid said: "they conceal." Qatada: "what they keep in their breasts." Ibn Zayd: "they gather from righteous and evil deeds." ﴿So give them the good news (fa-bashshirhum)﴾, i.e., inform them of ﴿a painful punishment, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward never to be cut off﴾, i.e., unreduced and uninterrupted.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 84, verses 1–25:

Makkiyya. It has twenty-five verses, one hundred and seven words, and four hundred and thirty-four letters.

Sa'id ibn Muhammad, Kamil ibn Ahmad and Muhammad ibn al-Qasim informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Mutar informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Shurayk related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us, saying: Salam ibn Sulaym related to us, saying:

Harun ibn Kathir related to us from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the Surah of Inshiqaq, Allah, glorified is He, will protect him from being given his book behind his back" [112] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/301.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿When the sky is split open﴾, and it listens to its Lord (wa-adhinat li-rabbiha), i.e., it hears the command of its Lord to split and obeys it, ﴿and it is right that it should do so﴾ (wa-huqqat), i.e., it is right for it to obey its Lord, and God has made that its duty.

﴿And when the earth is stretched out﴾, stretched like a leather hide of 'Ukaz, and its extent is increased. ﴿And casts out what is within it﴾, i.e., brings out what is in it of the dead and the treasures, ﴿and empties itself﴾, and becomes empty so that there is nothing in its interior. ﴿And it listens to its Lord and it is right that it should do so﴾. The scholars differed concerning the response (jawab) to His saying ﴿When the sky is split open﴾. It was said that its response is omitted because the meaning is understood. It was also said that its response is ﴿O man, you are toiling toward your Lord with toil, and you will meet it﴾, and its implied meaning is: when the sky is split open, every toiler will meet what he has done. Al-Mubarrad said: there is a transposition (taqdim wa-ta'khir), its intended sense being: ﴿O man, you are toiling toward your Lord with toil, and you will meet it﴾ when the sky is split open. It was also said: its response is ﴿and it listens to its Lord﴾, and in that case the waw is superfluous.

As for His saying ﴿you are toiling toward your Lord with toil﴾, the meaning is: laboring and striving toward your Lord through deeds, and you will meet Him, and you will be recompensed for it, whether good or evil. Al-Qutabi said: it means laboring in your livelihood toward the meeting with your Lord. Al-Kadh (kadh) means striving and exerting oneself in a matter until that matter leaves its mark, i.e., has an effect. From it is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever asks while he has what suffices him, his begging will come on the Day of Resurrection as scratches, or scars, or wounds on the face" [113] [[Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/589.]], i.e., the trace of a scratch. Ibn Muqbil said:

"And time is but two turns: by one I die, and by the other I seek life, toiling."

[[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 21/40.]]

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: Musa related to us, saying: Ibn 'Alawiyya related to us, saying: Isma'il related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bishr related to us from Sufyan al-Thawri, from his father, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The regretful one awaits mercy, the self-admirer awaits aversion, and every doer will come upon what he has done before" [114] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 15/936, no. 43607.]].

﴿As for him who is given his book in his right hand﴾, i.e., the register of his deeds, ﴿he will be reckoned with an easy reckoning, and he will return to his family rejoicing﴾.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Mandah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ghalib related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Sulayman related to me, saying: Mubarak ibn Fudala related to us from Ayyub, from Abu Malika, from 'A'isha, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever is reckoned with will be punished." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, has not Allah said: ﴿As for him who is given his book in his right hand, he will be reckoned with an easy reckoning﴾?" He said: "That is the presentation (al-'ardh); but whoever is scrutinized in the reckoning will be punished" [115] [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/127.]].

﴿But as for him who is given his book behind his back﴾: his right hand will be shackled to his neck and his left hand placed behind his back, so his book will be given to him with his left hand from behind his back. Mujahid said: his hand will be dislocated behind his back.

﴿He will call out for destruction﴾, i.e., he will be summoned with woe and ruin, ﴿and he will burn in a blaze﴾. Abu Ja'far, Ayyub, and the Kufans other than al-Kisa'i read it with a fatha on the ya' and light (tashdid-less) pronunciation, and Abu 'Ubayd preferred it because of His saying: ﴿except him who is to burn in Hell﴾ [[Surat al-Saffat: 163.]], and His saying: ﴿who will burn in the greatest Fire﴾ [[Surat al-A'la: 12.]]. The rest read it with a damma on the ya' and a shadda on the lam, and Abu Hatim preferred it because of His saying: ﴿Then into Hell roast him﴾ [[Surat al-Haqqa: 31.]], and ﴿and the burning of Hell﴾ [[Surat al-Waqi'a: 94.]]. ﴿He used to be among his people, rejoicing﴾. I heard al-Sulami say: I heard Mansur ibn 'Abd Allah say: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Misri say: Ibn 'Ata said of himself: "pursuing, striving."

﴿He thought that he would never return﴾, i.e., return to Us.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I seek refuge in You from returning after having been in order (al-kawr)" [116] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/148.]]. Ibn 'Abbas said: "I did not know the meaning of yahur until I heard a Bedouin woman calling to her daughter, saying: 'Hawri, hawri!' meaning: return." And the poet said:

"A man is but like a spark and its light: it returns to ashes after having blazed."

[[al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/330.]]

Then He said: ﴿Yes﴾, meaning: it is not as he thought. ﴿Yes, he will return to Us and be resurrected.﴾ ﴿Indeed, his Lord was ever seeing of him.﴾

﴿So I swear by twilight (al-shafaq)﴾. Mujahid and others said: it is the whole day. 'Ikrima said: what remains of the day. Ibn 'Abbas and most people said: it is the redness that remains on the horizon after the sun sets, and with its disappearance the beginning of the time of the late evening prayer (al-'isha') becomes due. Among the Companions who held this view were Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn al-Zubayr, 'Umar and his son, 'Ubada ibn al-Samit, Shaddad ibn Aws, Anas ibn Malik, Abu Qatada al-Ansari, Abu Hurayra and Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah. Among the Successors were Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Tawus, 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar and Makhul. Among the jurists were Malik, al-Awza'i, al-Shafi'i, Abu Yusuf, Abu Thawr, Ibn 'Ubayd, Ahmad and Ishaq. Others said: it is the whiteness, and this was the view of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz and Abu Hanifa. The preferred view is the first, because the scholars of the 'Abadila (Ibn 'Abbas's circle of Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Umar, Ibn al-Zubayr and Ibn 'Amr) agreed upon it, and because the evidences in Arabic speech and poetry attest to it. Al-Farra' said: I heard some Arabs say: "The thawr is red, as if it were the shafaq." And a poet said:

"Red in color, like the reddening of the twilight."

And another said:

"Rise, O boy, serving me without shame before time, with a cup filled with twilight."

[[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/303; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/275, where the text reads "murtabik" for "muhtashim".]]

The hollow is also called shafaq. The philosophers assert that whiteness never disappears at all. Al-Khalil said: "I climbed the minaret of Alexandria and looked at the whiteness, and I saw it moving from horizon to horizon, and I never saw it set." And God knows best what is correct.

﴿And by the night and what it gathers (wa-ma wasaq)﴾, i.e., what it gathers and assembles. It is said: wasaqtuhu, asiquhu, wasqan, and from it is said of a great collected quantity of food: wasq, which is sixty sa'; and a food that is wasq is one gathered into a sack or container. Mujahid said, according to the narration of Ibn Abi Najih: "what harbors in it of creatures." Mansur related from him: "what wraps and darkens upon it and enters into it." 'Ikrima: "what it has gathered in it of its creatures, scorpions, serpents, and its darkness." Al-Dahhak and Muqatil: "what it drives of its darkness; when night comes, every thing goes back to its shelter." Al-Ustadh Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib said: it is possible that on this view it is inverted (maqlub), because the root of saqa is yasuqu. 'Uthman: "it carries from the darkness." Abu Hayyan: "it comes from darkness or a star." Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "what it has worked in it." Ibn Abi Mulayka and Ibn Jubayr related from Ibn 'Abbas: "what it gathers," and he said: "Have you not heard the poet's saying:

'Indeed for us are she-camels, noble, gathered, which, if they found a driver, would be driven together.'"

[[Tafsir Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/150; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/277; Lisan al-'Arab: 10/380.]]

﴿By the moon when it becomes full (idha ittasaq)﴾, i.e., when it gathers, aligns, and its light is complete. Qatada: "when it becomes round." It is also said: "it travels." Murra al-Hamdani: "it rises, and that is in the bright nights." It is said: ittasaqa al-shay' when it follows in succession, and istawsaqa al-ibl when the camels gather and join together; it is an ifta'ala form from al-wasq.

﴿You will surely embark (la-tarkabunna)﴾: the readers of Mecca and Kufa, except 'Asim, read it with a fatha on the ta', and this is the reading of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ibn Mas'ud and his companions, Ibn 'Abbas and Abu al-'Aliya. They said: it means, O Muhammad, you will ascend heaven after heaven, degree after degree, and rank after rank. It was also said: it refers to the sky changing color after color, becoming at times like molten brass (al-dihan) and at times like dregs of oil (al-muhl), and being split open with the clouds at one time and folded (in the Tabari: "reddened") at another [[See Tafsir al-Tabari: 30/155.]]. The others read it with a damma and preferred it, Abu 'Ubayd said: "because the meaning is more apt for people than for the Prophet (ﷺ). Before the verse He mentioned those from among them who are given their book in their right or left hand, then He said after it: ﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe?﴾ and mentioned their mounting of layer upon layer, between them."

The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of the verse. Most of them said: state after state and matter after matter in the stations of the Resurrection, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from al-Kalbi. Hayyan from him: "at one time they recognize, at another they are ignorant." Muqatil: "that is death, then life, then death, then life." 'Ata: "at one time poverty, at another wealth." 'Amr ibn Dinar from Ibn 'Abbas: "the hardships and terrors: death, then resurrection, then the reckoning." The Arabs say of one who has fallen into a severe matter: "he has fallen into the daughters of Tabaq, and then into another set of daughters of Tabaq." Abu 'Ubayda: "you will embark upon the ways and conditions of those who came before you and of your own states." 'Ikrima: "state after state." (Another report:) an infant, then a weaned child, then a youth, then a young man, then an old man. The philosophers said: a human passes through, from being a drop of semen until he grows old and dies, thirty-seven states corresponding to thirty-seven names: a drop, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, then another creation, then a fetus, then a newborn, then a suckling, then one weaned, then a youth (yafi'), then one growing up (nash'), then one who is shooting up (mutara'ri'), then a hazur (a boy when he has grown strong and become capable of service; see Lisan al-'Arab: 4/187), then one approaching puberty (murahiq), then one who has reached maturity (muhtalim), then an adult (baligh), then a beardless youth (amrad), then one whose beard has begun (tarid), then one whose beard has come in (tari), then one with a sprouting beard (baqil), then one who has taken control (musaytir), then one whose face is full (mutarkhim), then one whose beard is thick (mukhtat), then one with a full beard (sumul), then one with a bearded face (multihin), then one who has come to his full stature (mustawi), then one who has risen (mus'id), then one who has gathered his strength (mujtami'), and the young man comprises all of this; then one who is struck (malhuz), then an elder (kahl), then one whose hair is white mixed with black (ashmat), then an old man (shaykh), then one with white hair (ashyab), then one who is bent (hawqal), then one who is bent double (saftana), then one who is decrepit (haram), then a dead person (mayyit). This is the meaning of His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿You will surely embark﴾.

﴿Stage after stage (tabaqan 'an tabaq)﴾. The word tabaq in the language means state. Al-Aqra' ibn Habis said:

"I am a man who has milked the years' flanks, and the years have driven me from one tabaq to another.
So I do not yearn for a companion who will part from me, nor does my inner being shrink from separation."

Abu al-Qasim 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Babi recited to me, saying: Abu Sa'id 'Uthman ibn Ja'far ibn Nusra al-Mawsili recited to us, saying: Abu Ya'la Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Muthanna recited to us:

"Patience is more beautiful, and the world is grieving: who among us has not tasted of its life a turbid draught?
When a tabaq of its joys is clear for you, time brings you a tabaq of its miseries."

[[Al-Ranaq: turbidity. Both verses are in Majma' al-Bayan: 10/303.]]

Makhul said concerning this verse: "Every twenty years they experience a matter they had not been in." This is the strongest proof of the createdness of the world and the affirmation of the Creator. The wise said: whoever is in one state today and another tomorrow should know that his management has been handed over to another. It was said to Abu Bakr al-Warraq: "What is the proof that this world has a Maker?" He said:

"The changing of states, the weakness of power, the frailty of limbs, the subjugation of strength, and the breaking of resolve."

I heard Abu al-Qasim the exegete say: I heard Abu al-Fadl Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Hamdun al-Nasawi say: I heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Arziyani say: Abu al-Fam 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd al-'Alawi entered upon the sick in Tabaristan and recited:

"I have become ill, though you were not ill with afflictions; thus is time, in which there is aloes and honey.
Indeed, the One whom the calamities do not touch, and whom neither time nor man changes, is God alone."

﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe? And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate?﴾ — i.e., they do not humble themselves or submit to it. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: they do not pray.

Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, by my reading to him, saying: Makki informed us by reading to him in the year three hundred and nineteen, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya related to me, saying: And in it (that year) 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Nafi' al-Madani read to me, and Mutarrif ibn 'Abd Allah related to me from Malik ibn Anas, from 'Abd Allah ibn Zayd, mawla of al-Aswad ibn Sufyan, from Abu Salama ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad, that Abu Hurayra recited ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ [[Surat al-Inshiqaq: 1.]] and prostrated in it, and when he finished he informed them that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had prostrated in it.

Abu Sa'id 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Nuh informed us, having read it to him in the year three hundred and eighty-six, saying: Abu al-'Abbas al-Siraj informed us, saying: Qutayba related to us from al-Layth, from Bakr, from Nu'aym ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad, who said: I prayed behind Abu Hurayra above this mosque, and he recited ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ and prostrated in it, and said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prostrate in it."

﴿Nay, those who disbelieve deny. And Allah knows best what they conceal (yu'una)﴾. Mujahid said: "they conceal." Qatada: "what they keep in their breasts." Ibn Zayd: "they gather from righteous and evil deeds." ﴿So give them the good news (fa-bashshirhum)﴾, i.e., inform them of ﴿a painful punishment, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward never to be cut off﴾, i.e., unreduced and uninterrupted.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 84, verses 1–25:

Makkiyya. It has twenty-five verses, one hundred and seven words, and four hundred and thirty-four letters.

Sa'id ibn Muhammad, Kamil ibn Ahmad and Muhammad ibn al-Qasim informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Mutar informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Shurayk related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us, saying: Salam ibn Sulaym related to us, saying:

Harun ibn Kathir related to us from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the Surah of Inshiqaq, Allah, glorified is He, will protect him from being given his book behind his back" [112] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/301.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿When the sky is split open﴾, and it listens to its Lord (wa-adhinat li-rabbiha), i.e., it hears the command of its Lord to split and obeys it, ﴿and it is right that it should do so﴾ (wa-huqqat), i.e., it is right for it to obey its Lord, and God has made that its duty.

﴿And when the earth is stretched out﴾, stretched like a leather hide of 'Ukaz, and its extent is increased. ﴿And casts out what is within it﴾, i.e., brings out what is in it of the dead and the treasures, ﴿and empties itself﴾, and becomes empty so that there is nothing in its interior. ﴿And it listens to its Lord and it is right that it should do so﴾. The scholars differed concerning the response (jawab) to His saying ﴿When the sky is split open﴾. It was said that its response is omitted because the meaning is understood. It was also said that its response is ﴿O man, you are toiling toward your Lord with toil, and you will meet it﴾, and its implied meaning is: when the sky is split open, every toiler will meet what he has done. Al-Mubarrad said: there is a transposition (taqdim wa-ta'khir), its intended sense being: ﴿O man, you are toiling toward your Lord with toil, and you will meet it﴾ when the sky is split open. It was also said: its response is ﴿and it listens to its Lord﴾, and in that case the waw is superfluous.

As for His saying ﴿you are toiling toward your Lord with toil﴾, the meaning is: laboring and striving toward your Lord through deeds, and you will meet Him, and you will be recompensed for it, whether good or evil. Al-Qutabi said: it means laboring in your livelihood toward the meeting with your Lord. Al-Kadh (kadh) means striving and exerting oneself in a matter until that matter leaves its mark, i.e., has an effect. From it is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever asks while he has what suffices him, his begging will come on the Day of Resurrection as scratches, or scars, or wounds on the face" [113] [[Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/589.]], i.e., the trace of a scratch. Ibn Muqbil said:

"And time is but two turns: by one I die, and by the other I seek life, toiling."

[[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 21/40.]]

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: Musa related to us, saying: Ibn 'Alawiyya related to us, saying: Isma'il related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bishr related to us from Sufyan al-Thawri, from his father, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The regretful one awaits mercy, the self-admirer awaits aversion, and every doer will come upon what he has done before" [114] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 15/936, no. 43607.]].

﴿As for him who is given his book in his right hand﴾, i.e., the register of his deeds, ﴿he will be reckoned with an easy reckoning, and he will return to his family rejoicing﴾.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Mandah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ghalib related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Sulayman related to me, saying: Mubarak ibn Fudala related to us from Ayyub, from Abu Malika, from 'A'isha, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever is reckoned with will be punished." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, has not Allah said: ﴿As for him who is given his book in his right hand, he will be reckoned with an easy reckoning﴾?" He said: "That is the presentation (al-'ardh); but whoever is scrutinized in the reckoning will be punished" [115] [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/127.]].

﴿But as for him who is given his book behind his back﴾: his right hand will be shackled to his neck and his left hand placed behind his back, so his book will be given to him with his left hand from behind his back. Mujahid said: his hand will be dislocated behind his back.

﴿He will call out for destruction﴾, i.e., he will be summoned with woe and ruin, ﴿and he will burn in a blaze﴾. Abu Ja'far, Ayyub, and the Kufans other than al-Kisa'i read it with a fatha on the ya' and light (tashdid-less) pronunciation, and Abu 'Ubayd preferred it because of His saying: ﴿except him who is to burn in Hell﴾ [[Surat al-Saffat: 163.]], and His saying: ﴿who will burn in the greatest Fire﴾ [[Surat al-A'la: 12.]]. The rest read it with a damma on the ya' and a shadda on the lam, and Abu Hatim preferred it because of His saying: ﴿Then into Hell roast him﴾ [[Surat al-Haqqa: 31.]], and ﴿and the burning of Hell﴾ [[Surat al-Waqi'a: 94.]]. ﴿He used to be among his people, rejoicing﴾. I heard al-Sulami say: I heard Mansur ibn 'Abd Allah say: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Misri say: Ibn 'Ata said of himself: "pursuing, striving."

﴿He thought that he would never return﴾, i.e., return to Us.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I seek refuge in You from returning after having been in order (al-kawr)" [116] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/148.]]. Ibn 'Abbas said: "I did not know the meaning of yahur until I heard a Bedouin woman calling to her daughter, saying: 'Hawri, hawri!' meaning: return." And the poet said:

"A man is but like a spark and its light: it returns to ashes after having blazed."

[[al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/330.]]

Then He said: ﴿Yes﴾, meaning: it is not as he thought. ﴿Yes, he will return to Us and be resurrected.﴾ ﴿Indeed, his Lord was ever seeing of him.﴾

Abu Sa'id 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Nuh informed us, having read it to him in the year three hundred and eighty-six, saying: Abu al-'Abbas al-Siraj informed us, saying: Qutayba related to us from al-Layth, from Bakr, from Nu'aym ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad, who said: I prayed behind Abu Hurayra above this mosque, and he recited ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ and prostrated in it, and said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prostrate in it."

﴿Nay, those who disbelieve deny. And Allah knows best what they conceal (yu'una)﴾. Mujahid said: "they conceal." Qatada: "what they keep in their breasts." Ibn Zayd: "they gather from righteous and evil deeds." ﴿So give them the good news (fa-bashshirhum)﴾, i.e., inform them of ﴿a painful punishment, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward never to be cut off﴾, i.e., unreduced and uninterrupted.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 84, verses 1–25:

Makkiyya. It has twenty-five verses, one hundred and seven words, and four hundred and thirty-four letters.

Sa'id ibn Muhammad, Kamil ibn Ahmad and Muhammad ibn al-Qasim informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Mutar informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Shurayk related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us, saying: Salam ibn Sulaym related to us, saying:

Harun ibn Kathir related to us from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the Surah of Inshiqaq, Allah, glorified is He, will protect him from being given his book behind his back" [112] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/301.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿When the sky is split open﴾, and it listens to its Lord (wa-adhinat li-rabbiha), i.e., it hears the command of its Lord to split and obeys it, ﴿and it is right that it should do so﴾ (wa-huqqat), i.e., it is right for it to obey its Lord, and God has made that its duty.

﴿And when the earth is stretched out﴾, stretched like a leather hide of 'Ukaz, and its extent is increased. ﴿And casts out what is within it﴾, i.e., brings out what is in it of the dead and the treasures, ﴿and empties itself﴾, and becomes empty so that there is nothing in its interior. ﴿And it listens to its Lord and it is right that it should do so﴾. The scholars differed concerning the response (jawab) to His saying ﴿When the sky is split open﴾. It was said that its response is omitted because the meaning is understood. It was also said that its response is ﴿O man, you are toiling toward your Lord with toil, and you will meet it﴾, and its implied meaning is: when the sky is split open, every toiler will meet what he has done. Al-Mubarrad said: there is a transposition (taqdim wa-ta'khir), its intended sense being: ﴿O man, you are toiling toward your Lord with toil, and you will meet it﴾ when the sky is split open. It was also said: its response is ﴿and it listens to its Lord﴾, and in that case the waw is superfluous.

As for His saying ﴿you are toiling toward your Lord with toil﴾, the meaning is: laboring and striving toward your Lord through deeds, and you will meet Him, and you will be recompensed for it, whether good or evil. Al-Qutabi said: it means laboring in your livelihood toward the meeting with your Lord. Al-Kadh (kadh) means striving and exerting oneself in a matter until that matter leaves its mark, i.e., has an effect. From it is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever asks while he has what suffices him, his begging will come on the Day of Resurrection as scratches, or scars, or wounds on the face" [113] [[Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/589.]], i.e., the trace of a scratch. Ibn Muqbil said:

"And time is but two turns: by one I die, and by the other I seek life, toiling."

[[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 21/40.]]

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: Musa related to us, saying: Ibn 'Alawiyya related to us, saying: Isma'il related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bishr related to us from Sufyan al-Thawri, from his father, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The regretful one awaits mercy, the self-admirer awaits aversion, and every doer will come upon what he has done before" [114] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 15/936, no. 43607.]].

﴿As for him who is given his book in his right hand﴾, i.e., the register of his deeds, ﴿he will be reckoned with an easy reckoning, and he will return to his family rejoicing﴾.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Mandah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ghalib related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Sulayman related to me, saying: Mubarak ibn Fudala related to us from Ayyub, from Abu Malika, from 'A'isha, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever is reckoned with will be punished." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, has not Allah said: ﴿As for him who is given his book in his right hand, he will be reckoned with an easy reckoning﴾?" He said: "That is the presentation (al-'ardh); but whoever is scrutinized in the reckoning will be punished" [115] [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/127.]].

﴿But as for him who is given his book behind his back﴾: his right hand will be shackled to his neck and his left hand placed behind his back, so his book will be given to him with his left hand from behind his back. Mujahid said: his hand will be dislocated behind his back.

﴿He will call out for destruction﴾, i.e., he will be summoned with woe and ruin, ﴿and he will burn in a blaze﴾. Abu Ja'far, Ayyub, and the Kufans other than al-Kisa'i read it with a fatha on the ya' and light (tashdid-less) pronunciation, and Abu 'Ubayd preferred it because of His saying: ﴿except him who is to burn in Hell﴾ [[Surat al-Saffat: 163.]], and His saying: ﴿who will burn in the greatest Fire﴾ [[Surat al-A'la: 12.]]. The rest read it with a damma on the ya' and a shadda on the lam, and Abu Hatim preferred it because of His saying: ﴿Then into Hell roast him﴾ [[Surat al-Haqqa: 31.]], and ﴿and the burning of Hell﴾ [[Surat al-Waqi'a: 94.]]. ﴿He used to be among his people, rejoicing﴾. I heard al-Sulami say: I heard Mansur ibn 'Abd Allah say: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Misri say: Ibn 'Ata said of himself: "pursuing, striving."

﴿He thought that he would never return﴾, i.e., return to Us.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I seek refuge in You from returning after having been in order (al-kawr)" [116] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/148.]]. Ibn 'Abbas said: "I did not know the meaning of yahur until I heard a Bedouin woman calling to her daughter, saying: 'Hawri, hawri!' meaning: return." And the poet said:

"A man is but like a spark and its light: it returns to ashes after having blazed."

[[al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/330.]]

Then He said: ﴿Yes﴾, meaning: it is not as he thought. ﴿Yes, he will return to Us and be resurrected.﴾ ﴿Indeed, his Lord was ever seeing of him.﴾

﴿So I swear by twilight (al-shafaq)﴾. Mujahid and others said: it is the whole day. 'Ikrima said: what remains of the day. Ibn 'Abbas and most people said: it is the redness that remains on the horizon after the sun sets, and with its disappearance the beginning of the time of the late evening prayer (al-'isha') becomes due. Among the Companions who held this view were Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn al-Zubayr, 'Umar and his son, 'Ubada ibn al-Samit, Shaddad ibn Aws, Anas ibn Malik, Abu Qatada al-Ansari, Abu Hurayra and Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah. Among the Successors were Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Tawus, 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar and Makhul. Among the jurists were Malik, al-Awza'i, al-Shafi'i, Abu Yusuf, Abu Thawr, Ibn 'Ubayd, Ahmad and Ishaq. Others said: it is the whiteness, and this was the view of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz and Abu Hanifa. The preferred view is the first, because the scholars of the 'Abadila (Ibn 'Abbas's circle of Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Umar, Ibn al-Zubayr and Ibn 'Amr) agreed upon it, and because the evidences in Arabic speech and poetry attest to it. Al-Farra' said: I heard some Arabs say: "The thawr is red, as if it were the shafaq." And a poet said:

"Red in color, like the reddening of the twilight."

And another said:

"Rise, O boy, serving me without shame before time, with a cup filled with twilight."

[[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/303; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/275, where the text reads "murtabik" for "muhtashim".]]

The hollow is also called shafaq. The philosophers assert that whiteness never disappears at all. Al-Khalil said: "I climbed the minaret of Alexandria and looked at the whiteness, and I saw it moving from horizon to horizon, and I never saw it set." And God knows best what is correct.

﴿And by the night and what it gathers (wa-ma wasaq)﴾, i.e., what it gathers and assembles. It is said: wasaqtuhu, asiquhu, wasqan, and from it is said of a great collected quantity of food: wasq, which is sixty sa'; and a food that is wasq is one gathered into a sack or container. Mujahid said, according to the narration of Ibn Abi Najih: "what harbors in it of creatures." Mansur related from him: "what wraps and darkens upon it and enters into it." 'Ikrima: "what it has gathered in it of its creatures, scorpions, serpents, and its darkness." Al-Dahhak and Muqatil: "what it drives of its darkness; when night comes, every thing goes back to its shelter." Al-Ustadh Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib said: it is possible that on this view it is inverted (maqlub), because the root of saqa is yasuqu. 'Uthman: "it carries from the darkness." Abu Hayyan: "it comes from darkness or a star." Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "what it has worked in it." Ibn Abi Mulayka and Ibn Jubayr related from Ibn 'Abbas: "what it gathers," and he said: "Have you not heard the poet's saying:

'Indeed for us are she-camels, noble, gathered, which, if they found a driver, would be driven together.'"

[[Tafsir Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/150; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/277; Lisan al-'Arab: 10/380.]]

﴿By the moon when it becomes full (idha ittasaq)﴾, i.e., when it gathers, aligns, and its light is complete. Qatada: "when it becomes round." It is also said: "it travels." Murra al-Hamdani: "it rises, and that is in the bright nights." It is said: ittasaqa al-shay' when it follows in succession, and istawsaqa al-ibl when the camels gather and join together; it is an ifta'ala form from al-wasq.

﴿You will surely embark (la-tarkabunna)﴾: the readers of Mecca and Kufa, except 'Asim, read it with a fatha on the ta', and this is the reading of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ibn Mas'ud and his companions, Ibn 'Abbas and Abu al-'Aliya. They said: it means, O Muhammad, you will ascend heaven after heaven, degree after degree, and rank after rank. It was also said: it refers to the sky changing color after color, becoming at times like molten brass (al-dihan) and at times like dregs of oil (al-muhl), and being split open with the clouds at one time and folded (in the Tabari: "reddened") at another [[See Tafsir al-Tabari: 30/155.]]. The others read it with a damma and preferred it, Abu 'Ubayd said: "because the meaning is more apt for people than for the Prophet (ﷺ). Before the verse He mentioned those from among them who are given their book in their right or left hand, then He said after it: ﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe?﴾ and mentioned their mounting of layer upon layer, between them."

The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of the verse. Most of them said: state after state and matter after matter in the stations of the Resurrection, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from al-Kalbi. Hayyan from him: "at one time they recognize, at another they are ignorant." Muqatil: "that is death, then life, then death, then life." 'Ata: "at one time poverty, at another wealth." 'Amr ibn Dinar from Ibn 'Abbas: "the hardships and terrors: death, then resurrection, then the reckoning." The Arabs say of one who has fallen into a severe matter: "he has fallen into the daughters of Tabaq, and then into another set of daughters of Tabaq." Abu 'Ubayda: "you will embark upon the ways and conditions of those who came before you and of your own states." 'Ikrima: "state after state." (Another report:) an infant, then a weaned child, then a youth, then a young man, then an old man. The philosophers said: a human passes through, from being a drop of semen until he grows old and dies, thirty-seven states corresponding to thirty-seven names: a drop, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, then another creation, then a fetus, then a newborn, then a suckling, then one weaned, then a youth (yafi'), then one growing up (nash'), then one who is shooting up (mutara'ri'), then a hazur (a boy when he has grown strong and become capable of service; see Lisan al-'Arab: 4/187), then one approaching puberty (murahiq), then one who has reached maturity (muhtalim), then an adult (baligh), then a beardless youth (amrad), then one whose beard has begun (tarid), then one whose beard has come in (tari), then one with a sprouting beard (baqil), then one who has taken control (musaytir), then one whose face is full (mutarkhim), then one whose beard is thick (mukhtat), then one with a full beard (sumul), then one with a bearded face (multihin), then one who has come to his full stature (mustawi), then one who has risen (mus'id), then one who has gathered his strength (mujtami'), and the young man comprises all of this; then one who is struck (malhuz), then an elder (kahl), then one whose hair is white mixed with black (ashmat), then an old man (shaykh), then one with white hair (ashyab), then one who is bent (hawqal), then one who is bent double (saftana), then one who is decrepit (haram), then a dead person (mayyit). This is the meaning of His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿You will surely embark﴾.

﴿Stage after stage (tabaqan 'an tabaq)﴾. The word tabaq in the language means state. Al-Aqra' ibn Habis said:

"I am a man who has milked the years' flanks, and the years have driven me from one tabaq to another.
So I do not yearn for a companion who will part from me, nor does my inner being shrink from separation."

Abu al-Qasim 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Babi recited to me, saying: Abu Sa'id 'Uthman ibn Ja'far ibn Nusra al-Mawsili recited to us, saying: Abu Ya'la Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Muthanna recited to us:

"Patience is more beautiful, and the world is grieving: who among us has not tasted of its life a turbid draught?
When a tabaq of its joys is clear for you, time brings you a tabaq of its miseries."

[[Al-Ranaq: turbidity. Both verses are in Majma' al-Bayan: 10/303.]]

Makhul said concerning this verse: "Every twenty years they experience a matter they had not been in." This is the strongest proof of the createdness of the world and the affirmation of the Creator. The wise said: whoever is in one state today and another tomorrow should know that his management has been handed over to another. It was said to Abu Bakr al-Warraq: "What is the proof that this world has a Maker?" He said:

"The changing of states, the weakness of power, the frailty of limbs, the subjugation of strength, and the breaking of resolve."

I heard Abu al-Qasim the exegete say: I heard Abu al-Fadl Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Hamdun al-Nasawi say: I heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Arziyani say: Abu al-Fam 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd al-'Alawi entered upon the sick in Tabaristan and recited:

"I have become ill, though you were not ill with afflictions; thus is time, in which there is aloes and honey.
Indeed, the One whom the calamities do not touch, and whom neither time nor man changes, is God alone."

﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe? And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate?﴾ — i.e., they do not humble themselves or submit to it. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: they do not pray.

Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, by my reading to him, saying: Makki informed us by reading to him in the year three hundred and nineteen, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya related to me, saying: And in it (that year) 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Nafi' al-Madani read to me, and Mutarrif ibn 'Abd Allah related to me from Malik ibn Anas, from 'Abd Allah ibn Zayd, mawla of al-Aswad ibn Sufyan, from Abu Salama ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad, that Abu Hurayra recited ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ [[Surat al-Inshiqaq: 1.]] and prostrated in it, and when he finished he informed them that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had prostrated in it.

Abu Sa'id 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Nuh informed us, having read it to him in the year three hundred and eighty-six, saying: Abu al-'Abbas al-Siraj informed us, saying: Qutayba related to us from al-Layth, from Bakr, from Nu'aym ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad, who said: I prayed behind Abu Hurayra above this mosque, and he recited ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ and prostrated in it, and said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prostrate in it."

﴿Nay, those who disbelieve deny. And Allah knows best what they conceal (yu'una)﴾. Mujahid said: "they conceal." Qatada: "what they keep in their breasts." Ibn Zayd: "they gather from righteous and evil deeds." ﴿So give them the good news (fa-bashshirhum)﴾, i.e., inform them of ﴿a painful punishment, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward never to be cut off﴾, i.e., unreduced and uninterrupted.

Sa'id ibn Muhammad, Kamil ibn Ahmad and Muhammad ibn al-Qasim informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Mutar informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Shurayk related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us, saying: Salam ibn Sulaym related to us, saying:

Harun ibn Kathir related to us from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the Surah of Inshiqaq, Allah, glorified is He, will protect him from being given his book behind his back" [112] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/301.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿And when the earth is stretched out﴾, stretched like a leather hide of 'Ukaz, and its extent is increased. ﴿And casts out what is within it﴾, i.e., brings out what is in it of the dead and the treasures, ﴿and empties itself﴾, and becomes empty so that there is nothing in its interior. ﴿And it listens to its Lord and it is right that it should do so﴾. It was also said: its response is ﴿and it listens to its Lord﴾, and in that case the waw is superfluous.

As for His saying ﴿you are toiling toward your Lord with toil﴾, the meaning is: laboring and striving toward your Lord through deeds, and you will meet Him, and you will be recompensed for it, whether good or evil. Ibn Muqbil said:

"And time is but two turns: by one I die, and by the other I seek life, toiling."

[[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 21/40.]]

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: Musa related to us, saying: Ibn 'Alawiyya related to us, saying: Isma'il related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bishr related to us from Sufyan al-Thawri, from his father, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The regretful one awaits mercy, the self-admirer awaits aversion, and every doer will come upon what he has done before" [114] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 15/936, no. 43607.]].

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Mandah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ghalib related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Sulayman related to me, saying: Mubarak ibn Fudala related to us from Ayyub, from Abu Malika, from 'A'isha, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever is reckoned with will be punished." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, has not Allah said: ﴿As for him who is given his book in his right hand, he will be reckoned with an easy reckoning﴾?" He said: "That is the presentation (al-'ardh); but whoever is scrutinized in the reckoning will be punished" [115] [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/127.]].

﴿But as for him who is given his book behind his back﴾: his right hand will be shackled to his neck and his left hand placed behind his back, so his book will be given to him with his left hand from behind his back. Mujahid said: his hand will be dislocated behind his back.
